50.0.0.en: 1- The mighty God, even the LORD, hath spoken, and called the earth from the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof.

50.0.1.en: 1- The writer prophesies about the incarnation of Christ and His coming in the fullness of time, for He is the Lord who is above all the pagan gods. Christ, the Word of God, spoke and called men from every place in the world to hear the good news of salvation. For He appeared in Jerusalem, which he describes as the perfection of beauty. Jerusalem is built on five mountains, the most important of which is Mount Zion, and therefore it is sometimes called Zion, as in this verse. The Jews and the Gentiles heard His good news in Jerusalem, and then the news of His preaching spread through the Apostles in the regions of the world from the rising of the sun to the going down thereof.

50.0.2.en: 2- He describes Zion as the perfection of beauty because in it is the Temple of God, which is a type of the Church, where the Holy Spirit gives the salvation which Christ accomplished on the Cross, and bestows it on the believers in the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace.

50.1.0.en: 3- Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him. 4- He shall call to the heavens from above, and to the earth, that he may judge his people.

50.1.1.en: 1- God came with fire and tempest when He descended on the Apostles and the Church on the day of Pentecost, and spoke on their tongues in languages they had not known, and they began to preach to the people of God who came from all nations. And God called the heavens and the earth to judge His people, because the heavens are a type of the prophets who are in Paradise, and the earth is a type of the godly Apostles, who all declare that the Messiah has come and redeemed His people, and who judge the Jews who did not believe and call them to faith. And three thousand souls of the Jews did believe and were baptized by the hands of the Apostles on the day of Pentecost.

50.1.2.en: 2- These two verses also speak about the fearful Second Coming of Christ on the day of judgment with fire and tempest, and He calls heaven and earth to witness, that is, He calls the angels and saints who are in heaven, and likewise the godly who are still living on the earth, and all of them judge the people of God who did not believe, and they are driven to eternal torment.

50.1.3.en: 3- Fire is a type of the power of the work of the Holy Spirit and of the word of God, which burns up sins within the one who believes in Christ. The tempest is the work of the Holy Spirit that shakes the soul and returns it to its Creator. Fire and tempest also signify the tribulations that come upon the believers in order to draw them to God.

50.2.0.en: 5- Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice. 6- And the heavens shall declare his righteousness: for God is judge himself. Selah.

50.2.1.en: 1- God asks His angels to gather to Him the believers in His holy name, who have made His covenant upon the sacrifice of the Cross offered on the altar of the Church, His most holy Body and Blood; to gather them from the regions of the world to enter His heavenly Kingdom. These are those who lived in the fear of God and walked in godliness all the days of their lives.

50.2.2.en: 2- When God gathers His godly into His Kingdom, the angels who are in the heavens declare His justice in rewarding the righteous with eternal life. But the wicked He puts far from Him in the outer darkness, that is, eternal torment. Thus God the Judge completes His judgment of all mankind.

50.2.3.en: 3- The word "Selah" at the end of the verse is a musical pause that calls us to contemplate the justice of God and His fear, that we may keep away from every sin and keep His commandments.

50.2.4.en: May you place the day of judgment before your eyes every day, to prepare for it by repentance, prayers, love for all around you, and forgiveness toward everyone.

50.3.s.en: (2) God asks for sacrifices of praise

50.3.0.en: 7- "Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee: I am God, even thy God.

50.3.1.en: God calls His people the children of Israel to hear Him. Several things appear from His call:

50.3.2.en: 1- His concern to warn His people so that they do not continue in their sins.

50.3.3.en: 2- Although they have sins, before everything else they are His people for whom He cares.

50.3.4.en: 3- He reminds them that they are the descendants of Israel (Jacob), their father beloved by Him, so they are encouraged that they are near to the heart of God.

50.3.5.en: 4- That He is their own God, who cares for them, for He says "thy God," so they are under His care and providence, and they trust that they are near to His heart and beloved.

50.3.6.en: 5- God begins by encouraging and showing His love for His people before He testifies against their faults and rebukes them for them; it is a gentle method for drawing the hearers to listen.

50.4.0.en: 8- I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices or thy burnt offerings, to have been continually before me.

50.4.1.en: God bears witness that His people are committed to offering the sacrifices and offerings that worship requires. Therefore God does not rebuke them for any shortcoming in worship, but rebukes them for the formality of worship, which is not accompanied by feelings of the heart, such as repentance, humility and love for God; and God wants the love of His people, and their feelings, before outward worship. God accepted the sacrifice of Abel for his good feelings, and did not accept the offering of Cain because of his evil, and He rejoiced in the widow's two mites more than in all the gifts of the rich.

50.5.0.en: 9- I will take no bullock out of thy house, nor he goats out of thy folds. 10- For every beast of the forest is mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills. 11- I know all the fowls of the mountains: and the wild beasts of the field are mine. 12- If I were hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world is mine, and the fulness thereof. 13- Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats? He goats: what is meant is the male goats, or the kids.

50.5.1.en: The forest (wilds): the desolate place, or uninhabited, or mountainous.

50.5.2.en: 1- God declares that He has no need for man to offer Him many sacrifices as formal worship. God is not in need, for He owns all the animals which He created, which run on the mountains and in the wilds and fly in the sky. God does not hunger or need, because He is perfect in Himself, but He asks only for the heart of man and his love, and if this accompanies his sacrifices the sacrifices become accepted and beloved by God. For God rejoices to see His children coming to worship Him, loving Him.

50.5.3.en: 2- Perhaps these verses are an indication that animal sacrifices will cease, after Christ offered His blood on the Cross, and there was no longer need for the animal sacrifices that were a type of the sacrifice of Christ.

50.6.0.en: 14- Offer unto God thanksgiving; and pay thy vows unto the most High:

50.6.1.en: 1- God asks for sacrifices of praise, which are the prayers and hymns that man offers from the heart and lips, for God asks for man's love, and not formal worship. Likewise good works and the labors of service are sacrifices of praise. And the greatest sacrifice in the New Testament is the sacrifice of the Eucharist, that is, thanksgiving, which is Communion from the Body and Blood of the Lord.

50.6.2.en: 2- God also rejoices in the paying of vows, because they are an expression of man's love for God, and declare that man is not attached to material things but is attached to God, in addition to the fact that these vows help the needy. And the paying of vows is the fulfillment of man's love for God, and the carrying out of promises, and at the same time a becoming a stranger to the world and material things.

50.7.0.en: 15- And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me."

50.7.1.en: 1- If you love God by offering sacrifices of praise and offering vows, He opens His door to you to ask of Him what you want, especially during tribulations. And trust that God is able to deliver you from the hardest tribulations, so that you thank Him and glorify Him.

50.7.2.en: 2- The day of trouble is the day of judgment, on which man takes refuge in God to save him from destruction, and He answers him, because he loved God all his life by sacrifices of praise and the paying of vows, and brings him into the Kingdom to live praising God forever.

50.7.3.en: May you be aware of and understand the meanings of the prayers of the Liturgy when you take part in them, and so prepare your heart and move it on the way of love; and when at the end you partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord you receive power and blessing, and God rejoices in you.

50.8.s.en: (3) God rebukes the hypocrisy of the wicked

50.8.0.en: 16- But unto the wicked God saith, "What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?

50.8.1.en: 1- God reproaches the wicked, because in appearance they are servants of God, but in truth their hearts are evil; in their outward show they have made a covenant with God to be His and serve Him, but they speak about the statutes of God without the speech coming from their hearts, because they do not live in them and in their spirit, and consequently it has no effect on others, but seems heavy, because the Spirit of God is not in it.

50.8.2.en: 2- Why is a person concerned to hear the opinion of others about him, and neglects the more important, which is the opinion of God?! It is more fitting for him to hear the voice of God in him, to change and amend himself by repentance, and then after he is purified he can live by the commandments of God, and it is easy for him to teach them. Then the covenant of God turns from words on his mouth to living words in his heart and in his life, and people accept his teachings.

50.9.0.en: 17- Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.

50.9.1.en: 1- God rebukes the servants who do not act on His commandments, saying to the servant: you have hated My word which reveals your weaknesses, and asks of you My orders that you may live by them. You have hated to be instructed by them and to carry them out, and even neglected them, that is, cast them behind you.

50.9.2.en: 2- This wicked servant used to accept the easy word of God, but the hard commandments of God he rejected and neglected. He is not faithful in his submission to all the word of God, but chooses from it what pleases him; the conclusion is that he refuses instruction, that is, the commandments of God that instruct him.

50.10.0.en: 18- When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him, and hast been partaker with adulterers.

50.10.1.en: 1- When a person neglects the commandments of God he is stripped of righteousness, so it becomes easy for him to fall into any sin, and its enticements draw him. So when he sees a thief who tempts him to join him, he consents with him and steals with him. And if he sees adulterers he clings to them and commits adultery like them.

50.10.2.en: 2- The servant who does not act on the commandments of God, and only speaks of them, is unfaithful to these commandments, that is, a thief of the power of the word of God, and does not let it work in him. He is also a betrayer of the word of God by refusing to act on the commandments of God, for he speaks the commandments of God with his tongue, while his heart is occupied with the concerns of the world and attached to them, and this is what is called spiritual adultery; this deserves the rebuke of St. Paul the Apostle in (Rom 2:21-24).

50.11.0.en: 19- Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit. 20- Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother's son.

50.11.1.en: 1- Another sin into which the wicked servant falls is speaking evil, and deceit and lying, as the Jews did with Christ, for they accused Him of false and vain accusations. For the wicked speaks what is within him, that is, evil, because out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh (Mt 12:34).

50.11.2.en: 2- The impudence of the wicked increases, so that by his evil speech he wrongs his brothers and the sons of his mother. By brothers is meant all men, and by sons of the mother those close to him, such as the Christian who wrongs Christians, or his relatives in the flesh. By this he wrongs everyone without restraint or limit, that is, evil has taken control of him.

50.12.0.en: 21- These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.

50.12.1.en: 22- Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.

50.12.2.en: 1- God rebukes the wicked because he commits many sins while God is silent and long-suffering, to give him an opportunity to repent. But the strange thing is that the wicked thinks this is weakness on God's part, or that God agrees with his evil: "thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself."

50.12.3.en: 2- God threatens the wicked that if he does not repent nothing awaits him but the punishment of the day of judgment, on which God sets his sins before his eyes, that is, exposes him and discloses his sins before all men. And likewise He tears him in pieces and no one can deliver him from the hand of God. What is meant is that God, after He judges the wicked, casts him into eternal torment, in which no one can intercede for him, and he does not come out of the torment forever; and God means by this threat to warn the wicked, perhaps he will repent. God may also use this tearing in pieces during life, by way of trials, to call the wicked to repentance, as He tore His people in pieces by the Assyrian and Babylonian captivity.

50.13.0.en: 23- Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God."

50.13.1.en: 1- The psalm ends with praise of the righteous who offer sacrifices of praise, which are the sacrifices of the lips that praise God, or those who strive against sins and raise many prayers in toils and vigils, and all these are sacrifices of praise; in addition to all good works and service, and also every condescension, obedience and detachment, for these are man's sacrificing of his own will and his submission to God. So the sacrifices of praise are by word, and also by deeds.

50.13.2.en: 2- God also praises the righteous man who orders his way through repentance and spiritual striving to change his conduct and acquire virtues. By this striving he glorifies God, because he seeks the Kingdom and rids himself of the lusts and preoccupations of the world.

50.13.3.en: Be obedient to the commandments of God and submit to them, whatever toil they cost you, trusting that God will support you in carrying them out. And if you fall, rise quickly, and also thank God for all His gifts, and your heart will rejoice, and you will advance toward the Kingdom.
